claims.statement: The repository is a monorepo of independently versioned Python packages under libs/ with no root pyproject.toml; each package owns its own pyproject.toml, Makefile, and README.md, and contributors work inside the single package they are changing.

The standard per-package workflow is to cd into a package, run uv sync --all-groups to install the package plus all dependency groups, then use the package's make targets (test, lint, format) with make help listing available targets.

Package make targets invoke tooling through uv run and export UV_FROZEN = true so a stale lockfile fails the run instead of being silently updated; make test runs unit tests offline (--disable-socket) and in parallel (-n auto) with coverage.

libs/Makefile provides repo-wide fan-out targets (lint, format, lock, lock-check, lock-bump, bench-all) that iterate over discovered packages and run each package's corresponding target, stopping on the first failure via set -e.

Releases use release-please with independent per-package versioning: separate-pull-requests is enabled and each of the nine configured managed packages has its own release-type python, package-name, component, changelog-path, extra-files, and exclude-paths.

The release-please-managed manifest records independent current release baselines: libs/deepagents 0.7.18, libs/acp 0.0.12, libs/code 0.1.75, libs/talon 0.0.8, daytona 0.0.8, modal 0.0.6, runloop 0.0.7, vercel 0.0.2, and quickjs 0.3.7.

Release-please assigns a bump-worthy commit to components by changed file paths rather than Conventional Commit scope; an empty commit therefore has no component path and can fan out to release PRs for every managed package, which the release workflow blocks before release-please runs.

A bump-worthy change that also modifies lockfiles or real files in another managed component can create a release PR per touched component; the release scope check blocks lockfile-only and multi-component fan-out unless ci:allow-lockfile-release acknowledges it, without preventing the resulting releases.

When a release-please PR is merged, release-please detects the release title plus the component CHANGELOG.md change and dispatches the package release workflow; that workflow builds, runs pre-release validation, publishes to Test PyPI and then PyPI, and creates the GitHub release.

Before release-please recomputes release PRs, the workflow waits for every merged PR still labeled auto:release-pending; this avoids evaluating a manifest that has advanced while the corresponding tag has not yet been created, and unreadable release state fails closed.

The release publisher resolves an explicit release SHA and, on the normal path, rejects it unless that commit's package pyproject.toml declares the requested version; build and GitHub tag creation use the resolved SHA so published artifacts and tag identify the same tree.

The Code package's make check is a local CI-parity entrypoint: after linting, import checks, and unit tests it checks extras synchronization, version equality, and lock freshness; it treats only the SDK pin's stale status as advisory while propagating other checker failures.

On release PRs, the release dependency workflow removes editable local sources and resolves changed package manifests against public indexes with uv pip compile; ci:ack-release-deps leaves the check running in report-only mode rather than skipping its follow-up-release reporting.

The release build verifies that the target package version is not already published on PyPI and fails closed if PyPI cannot be reached or returns an unexpected status, preventing a duplicate or unverified version from entering the publisher stages.

Release notes generation is intentionally fail-open: a failed notes job does not prevent PyPI publication or GitHub tagging, so the resulting GitHub release can have an empty body that must be repaired after publication.

Adding a partner package requires coordinated registration across issue and label routing, CI, synchronized scope validation, release workflows and release-please, release notes, dependency maintenance, secrets, and, when sandbox-backed, Harbor and integration-test credential surfaces.

The release workflow isolates its minimally permitted build job from the privileged publishing and GitHub-release job, reducing exposure of publishing and repository-write credentials to the build stage.
External pull requests must link to a maintainer-approved issue or discussion and the contributor must be assigned to it before the PR is opened.

Every release-please release PR is subject to the curated release notes merge gate: release-bot drafts notes, @release-bot apply writes the package changelog and PR body, and ci:skip-curated-notes is the explicit bypass.

After release-please or its lock updater pushes a release branch with GITHUB_TOKEN, release-please explicitly dispatches the curated-notes check for every updated release PR so the required status is refreshed on the branch's current head.

For deepagents-code, a stale SDK pin is advisory on the release PR but is a hard publisher gate; ci:dcode-skip-sdk-pin is a deliberate release-PR escape hatch that is forwarded as dangerous-skip-sdk-pin-check only after positively confirming the label.

The aggregate Makefile resolves ACP locks with Python 3.14 and all other package or example locks with Python 3.12, while ACP declares support from Python 3.11 and Talon from Python 3.12; each package's lockfile records its declared floor.
ACP's released 0.0.12 version is synchronized between its project metadata and release-please-managed version marker; Talon's current project and version-marker value is 0.0.8.
When release-please changes package metadata on a release PR, its update-lockfiles job regenerates uv.lock files because release-please itself does not regenerate them.

The current deepagents-code source version is 0.1.75 in both project metadata and its release-please-managed version marker, its changelog records that release, and its exact deepagents dependency pin is 0.7.18.

Curated release-note automation derives every managed component's changelog path and release branch from release-please-config.json, and accepts a release PR only when it is open, targets main, originates in the same repository, and has a matching configured branch component and release title.

The curated-notes workflow runs trusted automation from main, does not check out untrusted release-PR content, and gates short-lived GitHub App-token mutations behind validation of the trigger and maintainer permission; applying notes publishes a non-force Git Data API commit.

The curated-notes check creates a check run on the validated current release head for non-PR refreshes and closes an in-progress refresh as failure if cancellation or timeout interrupts validation, avoiding a permanently pending merge gate.

The Python release-notes test shim runs the native Node helper tests and checks workflow triggers, permissions, trusted helper references, component coverage, and safeguards that keep untrusted comments from reaching repository mutations.
The Code lockfile records Python >=3.12,<4.0, deepagents-code 0.1.75 as the editable local project, and deepagents 0.7.18 as an editable ../deepagents workspace dependency.
